<h1>Autodrops</h1>

An autodrop is a temporary mute or unmute that fires on a musical boundary and
puts itself back. You cue it, it lands at the next timing point in the 16-bar
cycle, and at the top of the next cycle it undoes itself. There is nothing to
remember and nothing to press again.

They work at two levels: **sequencer autodrops** drop a whole sequencer, and
**row autodrops** drop one row of one sequencer.

<nav class="docs-contents" aria-label="On this page"><b>On this page:</b> <a href="#why-they-are-worth-cueing-rather-than-muting-by-hand">Why they are worth cueing rather than muting by hand</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#try-this-first">Try this first</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#when-your-press-takes-effect">When your press takes effect</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#quick-reference">Quick reference</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#sequencer-autodrops">Sequencer autodrops</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#row-autodrops">Row autodrops</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#view-81-the-autodrop-view">View 8.1: the autodrop view</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#cc-autodrop-sweeps">CC autodrop sweeps</a><span class="sep" aria-hidden="true"> · </span><a href="#limitations">Limitations</a></nav>

---

## Why they are worth cueing rather than muting by hand

Because the length of the drop comes from *when* you press. Every autodrop ends
at the same place, bar 0 of the next cycle, and starts at whichever timing point
comes next, so a cue placed early in the cycle produces a long absence and one
placed near the end produces a quick fill. Pressing later gets you a shorter
drop, which means you can accelerate a passage by pressing the same button
faster, and none of it needs counting: the cycle does the timing.

The inversion is the other half. A muted row autodrops **in** rather than out,
so the same gesture that drops a busy row for eight bars brings a silent row in
for four.

## Try this first

1. Get a sequencer playing, unmuted.
2. Press its button on the **LaunchControl bottom row**. Nothing happens yet:
   the button starts flashing, which means the drop is cued.
3. Wait. At the next timing point the sequencer goes silent and the button goes
   solid.
4. At the top of the next 16-bar cycle it comes back on its own.

Then do it again in the last bar of the cycle and hear how much shorter the
drop is. That is the whole feature.

To take it back before it fires, press the sequencer's **top-row** button, which
cancels the cue and leaves the sequencer playing.

---

## When your press takes effect

Sequencer and row autodrops share the same timing. Nothing happens the moment
you press: the cue sits flashing until the cycle reaches one of six points, and
only then does the drop start.

| Point in the cycle | What happens there |
|---|---|
| **Bar 0** | Cued drops start, **and** every drop already running ends. Cued mutes and unmutes also resolve here. |
| **Bar 8** | Cued drops start. 8-bar cued mutes resolve. |
| **Bar 12** | Cued drops start. |
| **Bar 15, steps 1, 9 and 13** | Cued drops start. |

Two consequences worth holding on to:

- **Bar 0 is the only place a drop ends.** However late in the cycle a drop
  begins, it finishes at the next bar 0, so pressing later gives you a shorter
  drop. That is the acceleration effect: cue early for a long absence, cue near
  the end of the cycle for a quick fill.
- **The 16-bar autodrop is the exception.** It starts only at bar 0, never at
  the intermediate points, which is what makes it last a full cycle.

The drop lengths that come out of that, for a row or a sequencer:

| Cue flips to active at | Reverts at | Drop duration |
|------------------------|-------------|---------------|
| Bar 0 | next bar 0 | 16 bars |
| Bar 8 | next bar 0 | 8 bars |
| Bar 12 | next bar 0 | 4 bars |
| Bar 15 step 1 | next bar 0 | 1 bar (16 steps) |
| Bar 15 step 9 | next bar 0 | 8 steps |
| Bar 15 step 13 | next bar 0 | 4 steps |

---

## Quick reference

| What | Controller | Modifier | Effect |
|------|-----------|----------|--------|
| Sequencer mute autodrop | LC bottom row | None | Temporarily mute whole sequencer |
| Sequencer 16-bar autodrop | LC bottom row | REC ARM | Temporarily mute for full 16-bar cycle |
| Sequencer CC autodrop | LC bottom row | SHIFT + SOLO | Cue a CC drop (see *Limitations*) |
| Row autodrop (muted→in) | Launchpad col 9 | SHIFT | Temporarily bring muted row in |
| Row autodrop (active→out) | Launchpad col 9 | SHIFT | Temporarily drop active row out |
| Manual sequencer cue (any flavour) | View 8.1 | none (row chooses flavour) | Direct mute/CC/note cue |
| Manual TR-8 voice cue | View 8.1 RHS cols 5–6 | none | Cue a TR-8 voice for autodrop |
| Per-seq autodrop eligibility | View 8.1 row 8 | none | Toggle whether automatic cycles may drop that seq |

## Sequencer autodrops

Sequencer autodrops are cued from the **LaunchControl XL bottom row**, one
button per sequencer. They temporarily mute a playing sequencer for a portion of
the 16-bar cycle, then unmute it.

### The three gestures

| Modifier held | Button | Effect |
|---------------|--------|--------|
| None | Bottom row | Cue **mute autodrop** at next autodrop timing point |
| REC ARM | Bottom row | Cue **16-bar mute autodrop** at next 16-bar boundary |
| SHIFT + SOLO | Bottom row | Cue **CC autodrop** at next autodrop timing point |

### Cancelling and replacing

Pressing the **top-row** button for that sequencer while a cue is pending
cancels the autodrop and returns the sequencer to unmuted. Pressing the same
bottom-row button again either cancels or replaces the cue, depending on what is
already pending:

**No modifier, and REC ARM, both follow the same table:**

| Current state | Result |
|---------------|--------|
| Unmuted (or any active autodrop) | Cue the autodrop |
| Already cued for 16-bar autodrop | Cancel, returning the sequencer to unmuted |
| Otherwise cued for any autodrop | Replace with this flavour |
| Muted | No effect |

**SHIFT + SOLO** hands the request to the autodrop engine instead of writing a
mute state directly, so it follows its own rules:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Nothing cued on that sequencer | Cue a CC autodrop, length chosen from the current position in the cycle |
| Already cued as CC | Cancel the cue |
| Already cued as another flavour | Replace it |
| A drop already in flight | Press rejected: a running drop is not cancellable |
| Pressed in a dead zone of the cycle | Nothing happens (no length resolves there) |

Unlike the other two gestures, the drop length here is not fixed: it comes from
where you are in the 16-bar cycle when you press, the same rule the view-8.1
manual cues use.

### What the LEDs do

| State | Top row LED | Bottom row LED |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| Mute autodrop cued | Flashing green/off | Flashing off/red |
| Mute autodrop active | Yellow | Red |
| 16-bar autodrop cued | Flashing green/off | Flashing off/red |
| 16-bar autodrop active | Yellow | Red |
| CC autodrop cued | Green | Flashing off/yellow |
| CC autodrop active | Green | Yellow |
| Note autodrop cued | Green | Flashing off/orange |
| Note autodrop active | Green | Orange |

### State transitions

Each autodrop type is a two-step chain: **cue → active → resolved**.

| Cued state | Active state | Resolved state |
|------------|-------------|----------------|
| Mute autodrop cued | Mute autodrop active (sequencer silenced) | Unmuted |
| 16-bar autodrop cued | 16-bar autodrop active (sequencer silenced) | Unmuted |
| CC autodrop cued | CC autodrop active (see *Limitations*) | Unmuted |
| Note autodrop cued | Note autodrop active (see *Limitations*) | Unmuted |

Standard autodrops fire at bar 0, bar 8, bar 12, or bar 15 steps 1/9/13,
whichever comes next, and resolve back to Unmuted **only at the next bar 0**,
never at an intermediate timing point. The 16-bar autodrop fires only at bar 0.
8-bar cued mutes also resolve at bar 8, but those are regular mutes rather than
autodrops (see [Mutes and row states](/documentation/MSEQ/mutes)).

---

## Row autodrops

Row autodrops are cued from the **Launchpad mute column** (column 9, the
rightmost column of the LHS pad). Hold **SHIFT** and press a row's mute button
to cue one; press again with SHIFT held to cancel it.

They are symmetric but inverted, which is the point of them:

- A **muted** row autodrops **in**: it plays for the length of the drop, then
  goes back to muted. Use this to bring a row in for a fill.
- An **active** row (unmuted, drone or legato) autodrops **out**: it goes silent
  for the length of the drop, then returns to the mode it was in. Use this for a
  brief break.

| Current row state | Cued state | Effect |
|-------------------|------------|--------|
| **Muted** (or any muted-cued variant) | Muted, autodrop cued | Row temporarily **comes in** (plays), then returns to muted |
| **Drone** (or any drone-cued variant) | Drone, autodrop cued | Row temporarily **drops out** (silenced), then returns to drone |
| **Legato** (or any legato-cued variant) | Legato, autodrop cued | Row temporarily **drops out** (silenced), then returns to legato |
| **Unmuted** (or any unmuted-cued variant) | Unmuted, autodrop cued | Row temporarily **drops out** (silenced), then returns to unmuted |

Cancelling returns the row to its clean base state (MUTED, DRONE, LEGATO or
UNMUTED).

### State transitions

**Step 1: the cue fires and the row flips:**

| From (cued) | To (active) | Effect |
|-------------|-------------|--------|
| Muted, autodrop cued | Autodropped in | Was silent → **temporarily plays** |
| Drone, autodrop cued | Drone, autodropped out | Was droning → **temporarily silent** |
| Legato, autodrop cued | Legato, autodropped out | Was legato → **temporarily silent** |
| Unmuted, autodrop cued | Unmuted, autodropped out | Was playing → **temporarily silent** |

**Step 2: the drop reverts at bar 0:**

| From (active) | To (reverted) | Effect |
|---------------|---------------|--------|
| Autodropped in | Muted | Back to silent |
| Drone, autodropped out | Drone | Back to droning |
| Legato, autodropped out | Legato | Back to legato |
| Unmuted, autodropped out | Unmuted | Back to normal play |

Row LED colours for each of these states are in the "Row LED colours" section of
[Mutes and row states](/documentation/MSEQ/mutes).

---

## View 8.1: the autodrop view

A modifier-free manual-cue surface on the Launchpad that complements the LC
bottom row. Reach it with the col-9 view selector; it renders on both LPs of
both players.

| Cell | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| LHS row 8 cols 1–7 | Toggle autodrop eligibility for seqs 1–7 |
| LHS row 7 cols 1–7 | Cue mute autodrop for seqs 1–7 (re-press cancels) |
| LHS row 6 cols 1–7 | Cue CC autodrop for seqs 1–7 |
| LHS row 5 cols 1–7 | Cue note autodrop for seqs 1–7 |
| LHS rows 1–4, col 8, col 9 | No-op / dark |
| RHS row 8 cols 1–4 | Toggle autodrop eligibility for seqs 9–12 |
| RHS rows 5–7 cols 1–4 | Cue mute/CC/note for seqs 9–12 |
| RHS row 8 cols 5–6 | Toggle eligibility for the TR-8 bus |
| RHS col 5 rows 1–7 | Cue TR-8 main voices 1–7 (BD/SD/LT/MT/HT) |
| RHS col 6 rows 1–7 | Cue TR-8 alt voices 9–15 (RS/HC/CH/OH/CY) |
| RHS rows 1–4 cols 1–4, cols 7–8 | No-op / dark |

Voice 0 (the boom-tsk control row) and voice 8 (ghost RS) are deliberately
excluded: they are performance-mode cells, not autodrop targets.

**Colours.** Row 8 eligibility shows the sequencer's own colour when on, dark
when off. A sequencer-cue cell shows slate grey once that sequencer has at least
one active trig on an unmuted row, flashes its flavour colour when cued (tan for
mute, burnt orange for CC, yellow for note), and goes solid once the drop is in
flight. TR-8 cells keep their usual voice colours and flash purple when cued or
in flight.

**Cancellation.** Pressing a cued cell again with the same flavour cancels the
cue. Pressing a different-flavour row replaces the cue, provided the new drop is
at least as long as the one it replaces. A drop already in flight cannot be
cancelled: the engine rejects the press. TR-8 row cues toggle straight back on a
re-press.

Eligibility only affects **automatic** cycles. A sequencer switched off is
skipped by them, silently, but manual cues from this view or from the LC bottom
row still fire (see [Toggle views](/documentation/MSEQ/toggles)).

---

## CC autodrop sweeps

Automatic CC autodrops on the **master-bus slots (22/23/24)** ramp the CC rather
than jumping it. You hear a sweep **up** from 0 to 127 across the whole drop,
and then on the way out either a sweep **down** back to 0 (three times out of
four) or a hard snap to 0 (one time in four), so repeated drops do not all end
the same way.

The sweep follows the tempo, so it stretches and shrinks with the BPM rather
than running at a fixed speed. Pressing Stop in the DAW sends every active CC
back to 0, so nothing is left hanging.

---

## Limitations

Four things that are silent when you meet them, so they are worth knowing before
a set rather than during one.

- **CC and note drops do not silence a synth sequencer yet.** The intent is that
  a CC drop suppresses notes while letting CC through, and a note drop does the
  reverse. On a synth sequencer the engine treats both as unmuted: the cue
  times, lights and resolves correctly, and you still hear the notes. The two
  mute flavours work exactly as documented. TR-8 voices and the master bus are
  the exception, and do fire real MIDI.
- **Automatic cycles only ever mute a synth sequencer.** They never pick the CC
  or note flavours for you. View 8.1's manual cues are unaffected: you can still
  choose note or CC explicitly with a row 5 or row 6 press.
- **Sequencer 13 has no CC autodrop**, and sequencers 14 and 15 have none at
  all. On sequencer 13 the SHIFT + SOLO gesture falls back to a plain mute
  autodrop cue, exactly as if you had pressed with no modifier. On 14 and 15 the
  press does nothing.
- **TR-8 voice CC sweeps land on a placeholder.** The per-voice CC map is not in
  place yet, so a TR-8 sweep currently moves a placeholder controller number
  rather than the parameter it is meant to move.
